items.title: ExecuTorch WebGPU: export a PyTorch model once and run the same .pte file in Chrome and Safari
items.summary: ExecuTorch gets a WebGPU backend, so a model exported with torch.export runs locally in the browser tab with no conversion to another framework. Listed models include Llama 3.2, Qwen3, Gemma 3, SAM 2, Whisper and Real-ESRGAN, with on-device LoRA fine-tuning.

items.title: vLLM upgrades encoder disaggregation (EPD): 44-47% lower P90 TTFT on a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash multimodal benchmark
items.summary: vLLM's latest EPD work (metadata-only multimodal requests, Mooncake/NIXL embedding transfer, cross-encoder caching, router integration) reports 44-47% lower P90 time to first token and 6.6-9.5% higher token throughput per GPU, counting all encoder GPUs, at concurrency 64-128 on multi-page document inputs.

items.title: EgoForce dataset on Hugging Face: about 2,000 hours of egocentric video and hand motion paired with calibrated tactile force
items.summary: First subset of EgoForce is public: 40K episodes, 1,000 tasks and 1,000 demonstrators, aimed at force-aware human-to-robot transfer and dexterous manipulation. Paper and project page are linked, with more data to be uploaded.

items.title: Vals AI adds Watershed, a realistic AWS cloud scenario, to its CyberOffense eval; Opus 5.5 leads at 77.1% average
items.summary: Watershed simulates a Kubernetes cluster, ECS hosts and real cloud identities and policies. Across Nova, Lighthouse and Watershed, Opus 5.5 averages 77.1% and GPT-6 Sol Daybreak 65.9%; on Watershed no model earned all nine stages (Opus 5.5 averaged 55.7 of 100).

items.title: MiniMax H3 Image: 16 reference images in, 4K output in about 10 seconds, live on fal and Runware
items.summary: MiniMax's image model built on H3 supports edits with up to 16 references and up to 20 MP output, with a Highspeed variant at 2x speed, available through fal and Runware APIs on day 0. Runware describes it as open-weight.

doubt.pushback: A roster account says the Hugging Face license covers 'worldwide, excluding' the US, EU, UK and Korea, so the open-weight claim has regional limits; not verified against the license text.

items.title: Ornith 1.5 122B at 4-bit reported going from 91 to 242 tok/s on an M5 Ultra with a DFlash2 drafter, output identical
items.summary: A single-user test of speculative decoding with a DFlash2 drafter on Mac, reported token-for-token identical output, with the gain dropping to about 20% at four concurrent chats. No repo link or method shown; Mac support credited to two other builders.

doubt.pushback: Single self-run test with no code, config or settings shown; posted minutes before this sweep.

items.title: NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge reportedly uses DFlash 2 to speed up in-car reasoning
items.summary: A DFlash 2 author says NVIDIA DRIVE's Alpamayo 2 Edge uses it for faster on-vehicle reasoning, and points to the FlashDrive CoRL 2026 paper for going faster still. No numbers in the post.

doubt.pushback: No latency or accuracy figures given; the claim comes from the DFlash side, not an NVIDIA spec.
